runtime_acceptance.runtime: Directus 12.1.1 pinned image with kokonut_directus_runtime against the isolated populated clone
runtime_acceptance.diagnosis: The Field Worker policy has a custom source_system item filter for farm_activity read, custom create field restrictions, and a draft-only update filter plus field restrictions. The pinned Directus API returns no effective farm_activity permission and denies own and cross-scope requests. Directus 12.1.1 source filters stored custom permission rows when the custom-permission entitlement is unavailable; official documentation also states that unlicensed APIs hide stored permissions using filters, field restrictions, validation, or presets. The permission-compatible field_note read confirms the mounted tenant hook enforces own-location access and hides a cross-location row. Do not broaden permissions to make the farm_activity API probe green.
runtime_acceptance.directus_license_boundary: No Directus license was configured in the isolated runtime. This acceptance does not establish that a licensed Directus runtime will enforce these rules.
still_required: Choose whether Directus operational users will have a valid custom-permission license or whether all operational CRUD stays behind the Kokonut Gateway with Directus retained as an optional admin surface.
If Directus remains an operational API, provide its license through the approved secret channel and rerun own/cross-location and field-level acceptance.
Verify create/update behavior, field allowlists, expanded relations, lifecycle hooks, and scheduled jobs under the selected Directus profile.

limitations: The Field Worker farm_activity permission was denied before the tenant hook could prove own-scope behavior. A separate field_note read test confirms the hook is loaded and provides own/cross-location row scoping for that compatible read policy.
Directus custom permission licensing, role/field/expanded-relation parity, create/update behavior, schedules, and production provider mapping remain open.
This evidence does not establish field privacy, expanded-relation isolation, RLS, provider login, schedule parity, or any MAN-CAP acceptance.
